title: Project Policy
description: A research project's declaration of which mathematics standards apply to it and at what level. Standard 1 governs applicability; Standard 19 governs evidence and attestations. Keys under `rules`, `applicability`, and `attestations` are canonical rule IDs (`category.kebab-case-name`) and nothing else. No other spelling has ever been valid in this repository: the alias mechanism exists in the catalog for forward compatibility and is empty by design, because choosing one spelling on day one is cheaper than reconciling two later.

standardVersion.description: The framework version this project is evaluated against, matching VERSION. An unresolvable version is a configuration error, not a compliance failure.

project.description: Project identity, carried into validator output as `project` (Standard 22 R5).

rules.description: Level per rule. A rule absent from this map takes the framework default for the declared standardVersion; a validator reports how many rules were undeclared so absence is never mistaken for a decision.

applicability.description: Whether a rule's subject exists in this project at all. First-class, and deliberately NOT an exception: `not-applicable` means the rule has no subject here, whereas an exception means the rule applies and the project is knowingly not satisfying it (Standard 1 R2 and R3). The two must never collapse into one mechanism.

exceptions.description: Approved, time-bounded waivers of rules that DO apply (Standard 20 R4). An expired exception is a compliance failure, not a resolution.

attestations.description: Recorded human judgement for rules the catalog says a human evaluates (Standard 19 R6). An attestation is EVIDENCE, not a waiver: it says the rule applies and is satisfied on human review. It never overrides an automated failure, never applies to a rule the catalog marks non-attestable, never reaches a rule that is `forbidden` and `nonExemptible`, and returns the rule to not-evaluated once stale or expired. Most of what these standards require is mathematical judgement, so this is the mechanism that carries the majority of the framework's real assurance.

mathematics.description: Domain configuration. Everything here answers a question the evaluator cannot answer by looking: where the claims ledger lives, which regimes the project is in, and whether it is working toward a major open problem. Nothing here waives a rule — applicability, exceptions, and attestations are the only mechanisms that do, and duplicating them under a domain key would give a project two places to say the same thing and one place to disagree with itself.

regimes.description: Which of the five regimes of Standard 1 R1 describe this project. A claim about the PROJECT, not about the standards: it stops being true the moment the project acquires the capability it disclaimed.

claimsLedger.description: Repository-relative path to the claims ledger. Defaults to artifacts/claims-ledger.md.

proofAssistants.description: Assistants this project uses. Scanning covers all three regardless; declaring them lets the audit report an assistant that is present and undeclared, and records what a reader of a formal claim is being asked to trust.

openProblemMode.description: Set to true when the project is working toward a major open problem. Turns on the especially high bar of Standard 17: the per-problem tracking record becomes required, and so do stopping criteria and reopening conditions. Written in the policy as `openProblemMode: true`. It is typed as a string enum rather than a boolean because the YAML reader deliberately returns every scalar as a string and leaves type decisions to this schema — an under-validating parser that guessed types would be a false green, and the enum keeps `yes`, `on`, and `1` from quietly meaning something.

openProblemsDir.description: Repository-relative directory holding <slug>/problem.md records. Defaults to artifacts/open-problems.

ruleId.description: Canonical rule identity: `category.kebab-case-name`, dot-separated, lower-case throughout, with no hyphen in the category segment. The pattern rejects any other spelling by construction, which is deliberate — the reference framework this toolchain is vendored from needed an alias mechanism to reconcile two spellings that had both been written, and the cheapest way never to need one is to make the second spelling impossible from the first commit.

level.description: Standard 1 R4 and Standard 20 R4. Levels are preferred over booleans because `true` cannot express a considered partial adoption.

note.description: Why this project selected this level. Not a substitute for an exception.

reason.description: Required. A not-applicable declaration with no reason is indistinguishable from a rule that was forgotten (Standard 1 R2).

reviewedAt.description: When this judgement was last examined. Not-applicable is a claim about the PROJECT, not about the rule, and stops being true the moment the project gains the capability.

revisitWhen.description: The event that would make this rule apply. Required in practice: `math-standards policy` reports `policy.missing-revisit-condition` when a not-applicable declaration omits it, because a classification with no end condition is a permanent exemption wearing a temporary label (Standard 1 R2).

status.description: Only `approved` establishes the requirement. `rejected` records that a human looked and found it unmet, which is a failure rather than silence.

evidence.description: What was examined. Required, because an attestation without it is an assertion rather than evidence — the thing this mechanism exists to avoid.

reviewedAgainst.description: What the reviewer actually looked at. The validator digests these paths and compares; when the digest differs the attestation is stale and the rule returns to not-evaluated, because the thing reviewed is not the thing that is there now.

digest.description: Digest of the reviewed paths. Omit it on a first pass — the validator reports the current digest so it can be recorded.

revision.description: Informational revision identifier. Recorded, never computed — provider-neutral by design.

approvedBy.description: Provenance. An exception nobody approved is a note (Standard 20 R4).

expires.description: Optional. Absence means the waiver is indefinite, which is a stronger claim than it looks and should be rare. An exception past its expiry is a compliance failure.

reference.description: An ADR, issue, or work item carrying the decision.
